title: KV ring allocator with passive hole coalescing and workload-aware placement
creator: Samir Kapoor
description: Goal: reduce long-term GPU memory fragmentation and per-request tail latencies by introducing a low-overhead ring-based allocation layer for KV cache allocations, combined with passive hole coalescing that runs opportunistically when hardware is idle. This change targets continuous-batching workloads (many short-lived KV allocations from streaming chat/generation), where frequent small allocations and uneven lifetimes cause fragmentation that increases resident memory and forces fallbacks or larger model quantization. The feature composes three parts: (1) segregated size rings (power-of-two ring buckets) to avoid internal fragmentation for small KV slabs, (2) workload-aware placement that colocates KV slots which are typically accessed together (same request/session) to improve cache locality and reduce cross-GPU traffic for multi-GPU shards, and (3) a passive hole coalescing pass that merges adjacent free regions by lightweight metadata remapping and, when necessary, moving cold entries to a CPU-backed staging slab with async transfer to defragment hot GPU pools.
acceptance_criteria: System maintains stable SLOs: median token latency no worse than +3% and P95 no worse than +7% under baseline batching mix
Measured GPU resident fragmentation (bytes lost to unusable holes) reduced by >=45% in the continuous-batch benchmark suite
Under a sustained 4k qps synthetic chat workload with variable sequence lengths, fallback rate to low-memory quantized model variants reduced by >=60%
No regressions in correctness: KV lookups and cache hits unchanged; unit and integration tests covering remapping and async move paths
Feature can be toggled at runtime via config flag and rolled back with zero-downtime in prod clusters
progress_updates: 2025-10-05: RFC drafted describing ring bucket sizing heuristics and metadata layout (doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/KV+Ring+Allocator+RFC).
2025-10-12: Prototype ring allocator implemented in the runtime shim; internal microbench shows 18% decreased allocation time for small KV slabs compared to baseline buddy allocator.
2025-10-21: Added colocated-placement policy prototype that tags allocations by request-session id; preliminary tracing shows 24% improvement in intra-request L2 cache hits for colocated shards.

2025-10-29: Implemented passive coalescing worker that only runs when GPU SM occupancy < threshold and no active continuous-batch windows are scheduled; initial run reduces visible holes by 30% but induces small 2-4ms jitter in low-load experiments.

2025-11-01: Integration test harness against continuous-batch workload completed; benchmark pipeline (bench/kv/continuous) updated. Preparing PR for code review (#https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1432).
decisions: Use ring buckets (power-of-two sizes up to 256KB) rather than fine-grained freelist per-size because it simplifies async coalescing metadata and reduces per-allocation overhead.
Passive coalescing approach chosen over aggressive background compaction to avoid perturbing latency SLOs during high-throughput windows.

Cold-entry evacuation path will stage entries in CPU pinned memory with batched cudaMemcpyAsync transfers to prevent stalling the inference pipeline; we will not use unified memory due to unpredictable eviction latencies observed in internal tests.
Placement will rely on a lightweight request-session affinity tag emitted by the batching layer; no global graph partitioning required for first iteration.
tradeoffs: Pros: significantly reduced fragmentation without frequent stop-the-world compactions; lower allocation overhead for common small KV sizes; better locality for request-scoped access patterns.

Cons: slightly more complex bookkeeping (ring head/tail pointers, per-bucket bitmaps) and small extra memory for metadata; passive coalescing occasionally introduces millisecond-scale jitter on low-load nodes.
Operational: evacuation to CPU-backed staging increases PCIe traffic; need to monitor cross-host network cost if we later move entries between GPUs across servers.
benchmarks: bench/kv/continuous: baseline vs ring allocator; 45% fragmentation reduction observed in nightlies on p4dn.24xlarge equivalent synthetic trace
bench/latency/streaming-chat: median +1.7%, P95 +5.1% under target config (passive coalescing idle threshold = 12%).
dependencies: ENG-79010 (telemetry: add per-allocation histograms and hole-size gauges)

Add a soft-degradation mode that reduces coalescing aggressiveness if jitter exceeds configured threshold in production telemetry.
Run cross-region multi-GPU sharded experiments to validate placement policy under inter-GPU NVLink and PCIe topologies.
